strengths_deep_dive: Penny Appeal USA excels in organizational governance and financial health. The charity's <cite id="15">85% independent board membership</cite> ensures strong oversight of its international operations. Financially, the organization is highly efficient in its development efforts, with <cite id="16">fundraising costs limited to $0.14 per $1 raised</cite>. This efficiency is paired with a <cite id="17">direct service delivery model</cite> that minimizes intermediaries. Furthermore, the organization has demonstrated a commitment to transparency by meeting <cite id="18">19 out of 20 BBB Wise Giving Alliance standards</cite>, including all standards related to governance and finances.
rich_narrative.summary: Penny Appeal USA is a humanitarian organization that provides essential aid to vulnerable communities across <cite id="1">10 countries including Palestine, Yemen, and Syria</cite>. Founded in 2016, the charity has rapidly established itself as a reliable vehicle for Muslim donors, maintaining a <cite id="2">perfect 100/100 score for Leadership</cite> from Charity Navigator. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">$7,168,898 in total revenue</cite> to fund its diverse portfolio of relief programs. These initiatives range from <cite id="4">clean water access (Thirst Relief)</cite> to <cite id="5">orphan care (OrphanKind)</cite> and emergency food distribution. The organization is <cite id="6">verified as Zakat-eligible</cite>, distributing funds across all eight traditional asnaf categories to support the poor and needy. While the organization saw a <cite id="7">revenue decline of 34% in FY2024</cite> compared to the previous year, it maintains a <cite id="8">resilient 5.7 months of working capital</cite> to ensure program continuity. Penny Appeal USA operates with <cite id="9">high fundraising efficiency</cite>, spending only $0.19 to raise every $1 of income. This allows the charity to focus on its <cite id="10">direct service model</cite>, which assisted tens of thousands of individuals with food, shelter, and water in the most recent fiscal year.
